ei.title: Literacy Gaps in New Food Alternatives
ei.subject: 수능특강

fullPassage: When we were investigating why Americans valued meat so much, we found widespread confusion among consumers about which foods are healthy and sustainable. As part of the project, we asked consumers to sort different foods in any way they thought they should be grouped. Participants ended up dividing foods into groups such as fruits, vegetables, and dairy. However, most consumers didn't know how to sort plant-based "milks" and meat alternatives. Interestingly, they didn't consider them as part of any typical food group. In addition, most people still don't understand (or trust) lab-grown or cultured meats. The reaction to lab-grown meats will likely be similar to the often negative reactions to and suspicions of genetically modified foods when they first came on the market. These gaps in literacy of emerging technologies hinder the successful implementation of products that could have environmental and health benefits.

questions.passage: When we were investigating why Americans valued meat so much, we found (A)[widespread / limited] confusion among consumers about which foods are (B)[healthy / harmful] and sustainable. As part of the project, we asked consumers to sort different foods in any way they thought they should be grouped. Participants ended up dividing foods into groups such as fruits, vegetables, and dairy. However, most consumers didn't know how to sort plant-based "milks" and meat alternatives. Interestingly, they didn't consider them as part of any typical food group. In addition, most people still don't understand (or trust) lab-grown or cultured meats. The reaction to lab-grown meats will likely be similar to the often negative reactions to and suspicions of genetically modified foods when they first came on the market. These gaps in literacy of emerging technologies (C)[hinder / promote] the successful implementation of products that could have environmental and health benefits.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) widespread=널리 퍼진, (B) healthy=건강한, (C) hinder=방해하다
det.analysis:
❌ ① limited — healthy — hinder: (A) limited(제한된)는 widespread(널리 퍼진)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ② widespread — harmful — hinder: (B) harmful(해로운)은 healthy(건강한)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ③ widespread — healthy — promote: (C) promote(촉진하다)는 hinder(방해하다)의 반의어로 부적절
✅ ④ widespread — healthy — hinder: 원문 일치. 소비자들 사이에 널리 퍼진(widespread) 혼란, 어떤 음식이 건강한지(healthy), 기술 문해력 격차가 방해한다(hinder) ←정답
det.tip: widespread confusion / healthy and sustainable / hinder the successful implementation

questions.passage: When we were investigating why Americans valued meat so much, we found widespread (A)[confusion / clarity] among consumers about which foods are healthy and sustainable. As part of the project, we asked consumers to sort different foods in any way they thought they should be grouped. Participants ended up dividing foods into groups such as fruits, vegetables, and dairy. However, most consumers didn't know how to sort plant-based "milks" and meat alternatives. Interestingly, they didn't consider them as part of any typical food group. In addition, most people still don't understand (or trust) lab-grown or cultured meats. The reaction to lab-grown meats will likely be similar to the often (B)[negative / positive] reactions to and suspicions of genetically modified foods when they first came on the market. These gaps in literacy of (C)[emerging / outdated] technologies hinder the successful implementation of products that could have environmental and health benefits.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) confusion=혼란, (B) negative=부정적인, (C) emerging=신흥의/떠오르는
det.analysis:
✅ ① confusion — negative — emerging: 원문 일치. 소비자 혼란(confusion), 부정적 반응(negative reactions), 신흥 기술(emerging technologies) ←정답
❌ ② clarity — negative — emerging: (A) clarity(명확함)는 confusion(혼란)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ③ confusion — positive — emerging: (B) positive(긍정적인)는 negative(부정적인)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ④ confusion — negative — outdated: (C) outdated(구식의)는 emerging(신흥의)의 반의어로 부적절
det.tip: widespread confusion / negative reactions / emerging technologies

questions.passage: When we were investigating why Americans valued meat so much, we found widespread confusion among consumers about which foods are healthy and (A)[sustainable / disposable]. As part of the project, we asked consumers to sort different foods in any way they thought they should be grouped. Interestingly, they didn't consider them as part of any typical food group. In addition, most people still don't understand (or trust) lab-grown or cultured meats. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) sustainable=지속 가능한, (B) suspicions=의심, (C) implementation=시행/실행
det.analysis:
❌ ① sustainable — endorsements — implementation: (B) endorsements(지지)는 suspicions(의심)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ② disposable — suspicions — implementation: (A) disposable(일회용의)는 sustainable(지속 가능한)의 반의어로 부적절
✅ ③ sustainable — suspicions — implementation: 원문 일치. 건강하고 지속 가능한(sustainable), 의심(suspicions), 성공적 시행(implementation) ←정답
❌ ④ sustainable — suspicions — elimination: (C) elimination(제거)은 implementation(시행)의 반의어로 부적절
det.tip: healthy and sustainable / suspicions of genetically modified foods / successful implementation

questions.passage: When we were ①<u>investigating</u> why Americans valued meat so much, we found widespread confusion among consumers about which foods are healthy and ④<u>sustainable</u>. As part of the project, we asked consumers to ②<u>sort</u> different foods in any way they thought they should be grouped. Participants ended up dividing foods into groups such as fruits, vegetables, and dairy. However, most consumers didn't know how to sort plant-based "milks" and meat alternatives. Interestingly, they didn't consider them as part of any typical food group. In addition, most people still don't understand (or trust) lab-grown or cultured meats. The reaction to lab-grown meats will likely be similar to the often negative reactions to and suspicions of genetically modified foods when they first came on the market. These gaps in literacy of emerging technologies ③<u>facilitate</u> the successful implementation of products that could have environmental and health benefits.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 기술 문해력 격차가 제품의 성공적 시행을 '방해한다'는 맥락. facilitate(촉진하다)는 hinder(방해하다)의 반의어로 부적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① investigating — 원문 일치. '미국인들이 왜 고기를 그렇게 좋아하는지 조사하고 있을 때'에 적절
❌ ② sort — 원문 일치. '소비자들에게 음식을 분류하도록 요청했다'에 적절
✅ ③ facilitate — 원문은 hinder(방해하다). facilitate(촉진하다)로 바꾸면 '격차가 시행을 촉진한다'가 되어 본문 논지와 모순 ←정답
❌ ④ sustainable — 원문 일치. '건강하고 지속 가능한 식품'에 적절
det.tip: These gaps hinder the successful implementation — 격차가 성공적 시행을 방해(hinder)한다

The reaction to lab-grown meats will likely be similar to the often negative reactions to and suspicions of genetically modified foods when they first came on the market. These gaps in literacy of emerging technologies hinder the successful implementation of products that could have environmental and health ④<u>benefits</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 참가자들이 음식을 그룹으로 '나누었다'는 맥락. combining(결합하다)은 dividing(나누다)의 반의어로 부적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① valued — 원문 일치. '미국인들이 고기를 그렇게 좋아하는(valued) 이유'에 적절
✅ ② combining — 원문은 dividing(나누다). combining(결합하다)으로 바꾸면 '음식을 그룹으로 결합했다'가 되어 분류 맥락과 모순 ←정답
❌ ③ alternatives — 원문 일치. '고기 대안(meat alternatives)'에 적절
❌ ④ benefits — 원문 일치. '환경적, 건강상 이점(benefits)'에 적절
det.tip: dividing foods into groups — 음식을 그룹으로 나누다(dividing)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 유전자 변형 식품에 대한 '부정적인' 반응이라는 맥락. favorable(호의적인)은 negative(부정적인)의 반의어로 부적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① confusion — 원문 일치. '소비자들 사이에 널리 퍼진 혼란(confusion)'에 적절
❌ ② grouped — 원문 일치. '분류되어야 한다고 생각하는 대로(grouped)'에 적절
❌ ③ typical — 원문 일치. '어떤 전형적인(typical) 식품군에도 속하지 않는다'에 적절
✅ ④ favorable — 원문은 negative(부정적인). favorable(호의적인)로 바꾸면 '유전자 변형 식품에 대한 호의적 반응'이 되어 의심 맥락과 모순 ←정답
det.tip: negative reactions to and suspicions of — 부정적(negative) 반응과 의심

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: confusion=혼란 (어떤 식품이 건강하고 지속 가능한지에 대한 소비자들의 널리 퍼진 혼란)
det.analysis:

✅ ③ confusion: 원문 일치. '소비자들 사이에 널리 퍼진 혼란(confusion)' ←정답
❌ ④ implementation: implementation(시행)은 방해당하는 대상이지 '발견한' 대상 아님
det.tip: we found widespread confusion — 널리 퍼진 혼란(confusion)을 발견했다

det.korean: alternatives=대안 (식물성 우유와 고기 대안을 어떻게 분류해야 할지 모른다)
det.analysis:
❌ ① consumers: consumers(소비자)는 분류 대상이 아닌 분류 주체
❌ ② participants: participants(참가자)는 실험 참가자로 분류 대상인 식품 아님
❌ ③ benefits: benefits(혜택)은 마지막 문장의 맥락이지 식품 분류와 무관
✅ ④ alternatives: 원문 일치. '식물성 우유와 고기 대안(meat alternatives)' ←정답

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 investigating과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: investigating=조사하다/연구하다 → examining=조사하다/검토하다
det.analysis:
❌ ① consuming: consuming(소비하다)은 조사와 의미축이 다름
✅ ② examining: examining(조사하다/검토하다)은 investigating(조사하다)의 동의어 ←정답
❌ ③ promoting: promoting(촉진하다)은 조사와 의미축이 다름
❌ ④ ignoring: ignoring(무시하다)은 조사하다와 반대 방향
det.tip: investigating = examining = 조사하다, 연구하다

det.korean: hinder=방해하다 → impede=방해하다/저해하다
det.analysis:
❌ ① accelerate: accelerate(가속하다)는 hinder(방해하다)의 반의어 방향
❌ ② sustain: sustain(유지하다)은 방해와 의미축이 다름
✅ ③ impede: impede(방해하다/저해하다)는 hinder(방해하다)의 동의어 ←정답
❌ ④ achieve: achieve(달성하다)는 방해와 의미축이 다름
det.tip: hinder = impede = 방해하다, 저해하다

❌ ① gradual: gradual(점진적인)은 성공/실패와 의미축이 다름 (속도)
✅ ② futile: futile(헛된/소용없는)는 successful(성공적인)의 반의어 ←정답
❌ ③ modified: modified(변형된)는 성공과 의미축이 다름 (변경 상태)
❌ ④ cultured: cultured(배양된/교양 있는)는 성공과 의미축이 다름
det.tip: successful(성공적인) ↔ futile(헛된/소용없는)

questions.passage:
(A) The company decided to <u>sort</u> all job applications by the date they were received, placing the earliest ones at the top of the pile.
(B) When we asked consumers to <u>sort</u> different foods in any way they thought they should be grouped, most couldn't classify plant-based alternatives.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 sort의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: sort: (A) 날짜순으로 순서대로 정렬하다 / (B) 어떤 기준으로든 그룹으로 분류하다
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 정렬하다 — (B) 정렬하다: (B)에서 sort는 그룹으로 나누는 분류의 의미이지 순서 정렬이 아님
❌ ② (A) 분류하다 — (B) 정렬하다: (A)는 그룹 분류가 아닌 날짜순 배열, (B)는 순서 정렬이 아닌 그룹 분류
❌ ③ (A) 해결하다 — (B) 분류하다: (A)에서 sort out(해결하다)의 의미가 아닌 날짜순 정렬
✅ ④ (A) 정렬하다 — (B) 분류하다: (A)는 날짜순 배열 정렬, (B)는 종류별 그룹 분류 ←정답
det.tip: sort: ① (순서대로) 정렬하다 ② (종류별로) 분류하다

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "the process of putting a plan or system into effect"

det.korean: implementation=시행/실행 (계획이나 시스템을 실행에 옮기는 과정)
det.analysis:
❌ ① investigation: investigation(조사)는 계획 실행이 아닌 정보 수집 과정
❌ ② confusion: confusion(혼란)은 실행이 아닌 인지적 혼동 상태
✅ ③ implementation: implementation(시행)은 '계획이나 시스템을 실행에 옮기는 과정'이라는 정의에 정확히 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ suspicion: suspicion(의심)은 실행이 아닌 불신의 감정
det.tip: implementation = 시행, 실행. the successful implementation of products

questions.passage: These gaps in literacy of emerging technologies __________ (hinder) the successful implementation of products that could have environmental and health benefits.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오 (1단어))

det.korean: 주어 These gaps(복수)에 대한 현재 시제 동사. hinder는 원형 그대로 사용 (3인칭 복수 → 원형)
det.analysis: These gaps(복수 주어) + 현재 시제 = 동사 원형 hinder. hinders(X, 3인칭 단수형)가 아님
det.tip: These gaps hinder — 이러한 격차들이 방해한다. 복수 주어 → 동사 원형

questions.passage: The reaction to lab-grown meats will likely be similar to the often negative reactions to and suspicions of __________ (genetic) modified foods when they first came on the market.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오 (1단어))

det.korean: modified(형용사/분사)를 수식하는 부사가 필요. genetic(형용사) → genetically(부사)
det.analysis: __________ modified foods 구조에서 과거분사 modified를 수식하는 부사가 필요. genetic(형용사) → genetically(부사)로 변환
det.tip: genetically modified foods — 유전적으로 변형된 식품. 분사를 수식하는 부사형 필요

questions.passage: When we were investigating why Americans valued meat so much, we found widespread confusion among consumers about which foods are healthy and sustainable. As part of the project, we asked consumers to sort different foods in any way they thought they should be grouped. Participants ended up dividing foods into groups such as fruits, vegetables, and dairy. However, most consumers didn't know how to sort plant-based "milks" and meat alternatives. Interestingly, they didn't consider them as part of __________. In addition, most people still don't understand (or trust) lab-grown or cultured meats. The reaction to lab-grown meats will likely be similar to the often negative reactions to and suspicions of genetically modified foods when they first came on the market. These gaps in literacy of emerging technologies hinder the successful implementation of products that could have environmental and health benefits.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 어떤 전형적인 식품군에도 속하지 않는다고 여겼다는 맥락
det.analysis:
❌ ① the genetically modified foods: '유전자 변형 식품'은 본문 후반의 반응 비교 대상이지 분류 범주 아님
✅ ② any typical food group: 원문 일치. '어떤 전형적인 식품군에도 속하지 않는다' ←정답
❌ ③ the successful implementation: '성공적 시행'은 마지막 문장의 방해 대상이지 분류 범주 아님
❌ ④ the emerging technologies: '신흥 기술'은 문해력 격차의 대상이지 식품 분류 범주 아님
det.tip: they didn't consider them as part of any typical food group

questions.passage: When we were investigating why Americans valued meat so much, we found widespread confusion among consumers about which foods are healthy and sustainable. As part of the project, we asked consumers to sort different foods in any way they thought they should be grouped. Participants ended up dividing foods into groups such as fruits, vegetables, and dairy. However, most consumers didn't know how to sort plant-based "milks" and meat alternatives. Interestingly, they didn't consider them as part of any typical food group. In addition, most people still don't understand (or trust) lab-grown or cultured meats. The reaction to lab-grown meats will likely be similar to the often negative reactions to and suspicions of genetically modified foods when they first came on the market. These gaps in literacy of emerging technologies hinder the successful implementation of products that could have __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 환경적, 건강상 이점을 가질 수 있는 제품의 성공적 시행이라는 맥락
det.analysis:
✅ ① environmental and health benefits: 원문 일치. '환경적, 건강상 이점을 가질 수 있는 제품' ←정답
❌ ② negative reactions and suspicions: '부정적 반응과 의심'은 장애물이지 제품 이점이 아님
❌ ③ plant-based milks and meats: '식물 기반 우유와 고기'는 제품 유형이지 '가질 수 있는' 혜택이 아님
❌ ④ lab-grown or cultured meats: '배양육'은 제품 유형이지 그 제품이 가진 혜택이 아님
det.tip: products that could have environmental and health benefits
